rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: The LCM of smallest 2-digit number and smallest composite number is
rows.solution:
The smallest 2-digit number is 10 and the smallest composite number is 4.

\(10 = 2 \times 5\) and \(4 = 2^2\), so LCM \(= 2^2 \times 5 = 20\).

This is option (C) \(20\).

rows.stem: The distance of the point \((-4, 3)\) from y-axis is
rows.solution:
The distance of a point from the y-axis is the absolute value of its x-coordinate: \(|-4| = 4\). (A distance is never negative.)

This is option (B) \(4\).

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: If one zero of the polynomial \(x^2 + 3x + k\) is 2, then the value of k.
rows.solution:
2 is a zero, so the polynomial is 0 at \(x = 2\): \(2^2 + 3(2) + k = 0\), that is \(4 + 6 + k = 0\) and \(k = -10\).

This is option (A) \(-10\).

rows.subtopic: Probability from a Collection of Objects
rows.stem: A box contains 90 discs, numbered from 1 to 90. If one disc is drawn at random from the box, the probability that it bears a prime number less than 23 is
rows.solution:
The primes less than 23 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19: 8 of the 90 equally likely discs.

\(P = \dfrac{8}{90} = \dfrac{4}{45}\), which is option (C) \(\dfrac{4}{45}\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Graphical Method and Nature of Solutions
rows.stem: The coordinates of the point where the line \(2y = 4x + 5\) crosses \(x\)-axis is
rows.solution:
On the x-axis \(y = 0\), so \(0 = 4x + 5\) and \(x = -\dfrac{5}{4}\). The line crosses the x-axis at \(\left(-\dfrac{5}{4}, 0\right)\).

This is option (C) \(\left(\dfrac{-5}{4}, 0\right)\).

\(\cos^4 A - \sin^4 A = (\cos^2 A - \sin^2 A)(\cos^2 A + \sin^2 A) = \cos^2 A - \sin^2 A\), since \(\cos^2 A + \sin^2 A = 1\).

Writing \(\sin^2 A = 1 - \cos^2 A\): \(\cos^2 A - (1 - \cos^2 A) = 2\cos^2 A - 1\).

This is option (D) \(2\cos^2 A - 1\).

rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: Find the LCM and HCF of 72 and 120.
rows.solution:
\(72 = 2^3 \times 3^2\) and \(120 = 2^3 \times 3 \times 5\).

LCM \(= 2^3 \times 3^2 \times 5 = 360\) (the highest power of each prime).

HCF \(= 2^3 \times 3 = 24\) (the lowest power of each common prime).

(Check: \(24 \times 360 = 8640 = 72 \times 120\).)

rows.stem: Find the points on the \(x\)-axis, each of which is at a distance of 10 units from the point \(A(11, -8)\).
In the given figure, AB and CD are diameters of a circle with centre O perpendicular to each other. If OA = 7 cm, find the area of shaded region.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - only the drawing shows which region is shaded: the two minor segments cut off by chords BC and CA (between each chord and its arc), with diameters AB and DC perpendicular at O. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
In the figure the shaded region is the two segments cut off by the chords BC and CA.

AB and CD are perpendicular diameters, so \(\angle BOC = \angle COA = 90^\circ\) and each of BOC and COA is a quadrant of radius \(OA = 7\) cm.

Area of quadrant BOC \(= \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = \dfrac{77}{2}\ \text{cm}^2\).

Area of \(\Delta BOC = \dfrac{1}{2} \times OB \times OC = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 7 \times 7 = \dfrac{49}{2}\ \text{cm}^2\).

The segment on BC has area \(\dfrac{77}{2} - \dfrac{49}{2} = 14\ \text{cm}^2\), and the segment on CA is the same.

Area of the shaded region \(= 2\left[\dfrac{77}{2} - \dfrac{49}{2}\right] = 28\ \text{cm}^2\).

rows.subtopic: Volume of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: A solid is in the shape of a right-circular cone surmounted on a hemisphere, the radius of each of them being 3.5 cm and the total height of the solid is 9.5 cm. Find the volume of the solid.
rows.solution:
The radius of the hemisphere and of the cone is \(3.5 = \dfrac{7}{2}\) cm, and the height of the cone is \(9.5 - 3.5 = 6\) cm.

Volume of the solid \(=\) volume of the hemisphere \(+\) volume of the cone

\(= \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times \left(\dfrac{7}{2}\right)^3 + \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times \left(\dfrac{7}{2}\right)^2 \times 6\)

\(= \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times \left(\dfrac{7}{2}\right)^2 \left(2 \times \dfrac{7}{2} + 6\right) = \dfrac{77}{6} \times 13 = \dfrac{1001}{6}\ \text{cm}^3 \approx 166.83\ \text{cm}^3\).

(Separately: the hemisphere is \(\dfrac{539}{6}\ \text{cm}^3\) and the cone \(77\ \text{cm}^3\).)

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: Find the sum of integers between 100 and 200 which are (i) divisible by 9 (ii) not divisible by 9.
rows.solution:
(i) The integers between 100 and 200 divisible by 9 are 108, 117, 126, ..., 198, an AP with \(a = 108\) and \(d = 9\).

\(108 + (n - 1)9 = 198\), so \(n - 1 = 10\) and \(n = 11\).

\(S_{11} = \dfrac{n}{2}(a + l) = \dfrac{11}{2}(108 + 198) = \dfrac{11}{2} \times 306 = 1683\).

(ii) The integers between 100 and 200 are 101, 102, ..., 199: 99 terms.

Their sum is \(\dfrac{99}{2}(101 + 199) = \dfrac{99}{2} \times 300 = 14850\).

Sum of the integers not divisible by 9 \(= 14850 - 1683 = 13167\).

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.solution:
The left side is an AP with \(a = -4\) and \(d = 3\), and x is its last term. If x is the nth term, \(-4 + (n - 1)3 = x\), so \(n = \dfrac{x + 7}{3}\).

\(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}(a + l) = 437\): \(\dfrac{x + 7}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{2}(-4 + x) = 437\).

\((x + 7)(x - 4) = 437 \times 6 = 2622\), so \(x^2 + 3x - 28 = 2622\) and \(x^2 + 3x - 2650 = 0\).

\((x + 53)(x - 50) = 0\), so \(x = 50\) or \(x = -53\).

\(x = -53\) would make \(n = \dfrac{-46}{3}\), which is not a natural number, so it is rejected. So \(x = 50\).

(Check: \(n = \dfrac{57}{3} = 19\) and \(S_{19} = \dfrac{19}{2}(-4 + 50) = 19 \times 23 = 437\).)
